page: Microsoft Azure E64-32s_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine utilizing a constrained-core architecture. Powered by the Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V, it provides 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores. The instance features a high memory allocation of 504.0 GB of RAM, equating to 15.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware instruction extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI support, AES cryptography, and Bit Manipulation Instructions (BMI2).

Architecturally, this configuration provides no bundled local ephemeral storage and includes zero dedicated GPUs, directing all disk I/O through external attached storage. Synthetic and computational benchmarks place CPU and memory throughput in the median tier, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 10498.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 29038.35. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 142.18 GB/sec with 83.44 GB/sec write throughput, supporting in-memory processing workloads such as Redis, which achieves 27.94 million SET operations per second.

Cost efficiency is centered around constrained compute licensing. By constraining the 64-vCPU host profile to 32 active vCPUs while retaining the full 504.0 GB memory footprint, the instance reduces per-core software licensing expenses for memory-heavy enterprise platforms. However, raw parallel computation and large-model machine learning inference remain restricted by the halved core count and lack of hardware accelerators.

The E64-32s_v4 is best suited for memory-intensive enterprise software, large in-memory caching systems, operational analytics, relational databases requiring constrained core licensing, and high-memory data processing tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure E64-32s_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine operating on the Intel Xeon 8272CL processor at 2.6 GHz, providing 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores alongside 504.0 GB of system memory. Designed as a constrained-core configuration, it delivers a high memory-to-core ratio of 15.75 GB per vCPU while reducing software core licensing demands. The instance includes AVX-512 vector support, no integrated GPU hardware, and no local disk storage, relying on external network storage. Benchmark evaluations show balanced computational throughput with a PassMark CPU score of 29038.35 and an uncached memory read bandwidth of 142.18 GB/sec. Memory-intensive transactional tasks perform consistently, demonstrated by 27.94 million Redis SET operations per second. The instance is suited for enterprise databases, in-memory caches, and memory-heavy analytics pipelines.
